in-terminal-thermal-emf.note: All five cited pages of 01258b re-read; all hold. p2: Seebeck coefficients on PCBs typically, but not always, below +-100 uV/degC; Equation 1; Figure 3 shows four junctions of an SMD resistor at a uniform +125 degC at 14/-5/5/-14 mV summing to zero, with the constant-temperature note quoted verbatim. p3 Figure 4: 1206, +125.0 to +126.2 degC at a 10 degC/in gradient, junction voltages 14.000/-5.001/5.011/-14.048 mV, total -38 uV - exact. p4: the inputs to an op amp should connect to the same materials, verbatim, plus Figure 6 resistors aligned with constant-temperature contour lines. p16: bench tests saw +-1 uV to +-2 uV due to the IC socket, do not use sockets for critical components. p17 callouts 2/3a/4: 0805 parts, arranged so that their thermoelectric voltages cancel, and metal fill connected to the ground plane minimizes thermal gradients at the cold junction connector. Specifically checked the known weak point: the record does NOT reproduce Table 1, whose values p2 itself calls arbitrary illustrative values, and invents no coefficient for the copper/tin/steel screw stack - it carries only the +-100 uV/degC bound and the -38 uV worked gradient case. Envelope +-10 degC is a real vendor statement but lives on p1 (response can be linearized over small temperature ranges, e.g. +-10 degC), which the record does not list as a source.

in-bias-current-return-path.note: Re-read ina333 p16 and p17 visually. Citations are accurate: p16 s8.2.2.5 gives approximately 100 Gohm input impedance, a path must be provided for the input bias current of both inputs, Ib typically +-70 pA, and the saturation sentence is verbatim (Without a bias current path, the inputs float to a potential that exceeds the common-mode range of the INA333 device, and the input amplifiers will saturate). p17 Figure 34 does draw all three claimed forms - microphone/hydrophone with a matched 47k/47k pair to a common ground node, thermocouple with a single 10k to ground, transformer with the grounded centre tap annotated Center tap provides bias current return. REFUTED on the failure signature. The prose asserts the output is typically parked near a rail. Section 8.2.2.6 sits on cited page 17, immediately under Figure 34, and states the opposite: Input overload conditions can produce an output voltage that appears normal. For example, if an input overload condition drives both input amplifiers to the respective positive output swing limit, the difference voltage measured by the output amplifier is near zero. The output of the INA333 is near 0 V even though both inputs are overloaded. slyt226 p1 column 1 says the same of this exact mode: Saturation causes the INA output voltage, although of wrong value, to appear normal to the following processing circuitry. The physics agrees with the vendor and not the record: both bias currents drive both inputs the same way, so the float is a common-mode excursion, both input amplifiers hit the same swing limit and the output amplifier sees near zero difference - the output parks near Ref, not near a rail. This is the one thing a reusable record about this failure is for, and it is wrong and contradicted on a page the record itself cites. TO PASS: replace typically parked near a rail with the p17 s8.2.2.6 signature (an output that looks plausible, near Ref) and add p17 s8.2.2.6 to the source notes. Everything else in the record holds. Minor, not the ground: the fourth entry in rule.legal_forms (source already referenced to that ground, third wire) is sound physics and the same mechanism as the grounded centre tap, but it is stated on neither cited page.

in-bias-return-sizing.note: Re-read ina333 p16 and p17 visually. The citations are clean and the page numbers are right. p16 carries the fork verbatim: If the differential source resistance is low, the bias current return path can be connected to one input (see the thermocouple example in Figure 34). With higher source impedance, using two equal resistors provides a balanced input with possible advantages of lower input offset voltage as a result of bias current and better high-frequency common-mode rejection. Ib +-70 pA typ and 100 Gohm are on the same page. p17 Figure 34 shows the 47k/47k matched pair and the single 10k. The witness question lands on the safe side: the record keeps the general sizing LAW in rule.upper_bound (R_bias x Ib against the offset budget), which scales with any input structure, and leaves the 47k/10k numbers in the source notes as the vendor examples they are - so the INA333-to-AD8226 substitution is legitimate here. REFUTED on the envelope, which is the record's own firing contract. Two defects. (1) envelope_note says of everything below its 10 kohm bound: below it (bridge, thermocouple, strain-gauge class) a bleeder pair is unnecessary. Figure 34 on cited p17 fits a 10 kohm bleeder to a thermocouple - a low-source-resistance floating source squarely inside the excluded class. The vendor's own figure contradicts the envelope note. The dim that decides whether the network is needed at all is whether the source gives a DC path to the amplifier ground, not the source resistance; source resistance only picks the FORM (one resistor or two) and the SIZE. The record's own sibling rule field source_referenced says exactly this, so the envelope contradicts the record too. (2) rsource_ohm is capped at 10 kohm and the record's own rule.high_source_resistance field prescribes the two-equal-resistor form for higher source impedance - so the record refuses to fire in the regime its own rule was written for, and the 10 kohm figure appears on neither p16 nor p17 nor anywhere in the ledger. TO PASS: drop or invert the rsource cap (the rule holds at all source resistances; only the answer changes) and rewrite envelope_note to key on DC referencing rather than declaring a bleeder unnecessary below a resistance. Minor, not the ground: the lower_bound (loading, Johnson noise) is real physics but appears on no cited page - the source notes do not claim it, so it is honest derivation, not a miscitation.

in-path-symmetry-sets-cmrr.note: Re-read sboa582 p4 and p5, ina333 p15 and slyt226 p1 visually. Transcription is clean and every page number is right: p5 carries the CM-to-differential sentence verbatim, Equation 7 CMRR_R = (G+1)/(4t), Equation 8 the parallel combination, and Figure 2-4 does show CMRR_R flat and dominant while CMRR_A rolls off at 20 dB/dec and crosses near 100 kHz; p4 carries R_absolute = R_nominal(1+t), the 995 to 1005 ohm span of a 1 kohm +-0.5 pct part, Figure 2-3 with 995/1005/1005/995 around an OPA387 specified at 150 dB typ, and the worst-case CMRR_D of only 40 dB. ina333 p15 is verbatim including the few-picofarads stability limit, and it is honestly labelled as being about the RG pins. slyt226 p1 really does frame passive RC at the INA input as lowering CMRR, and Figure 1 shows VCM passing the input stage at unity gain. REFUTED on three page-level points. (1) The worked case drops its condition. sboa582 Figure 3-2 caption fixes the worked circuit at Gain = 1 V/V, and 40 dB is just (1+1)/(4 x 0.005) = 100. The record's worked_case field states 0.5 pct resistors around a 150 dB amplifier give 40 dB of stage CMRR with no gain stated; at the gain this interface class actually runs, (151)/(0.02) is 77.5 dB, not 40 dB. A number quoted without the condition that produces it. (2) The topology substitution is not legitimate for the quantitative law. Every circuit in sboa582 (Figures 2-1, 2-3, 3-1, 3-2, and the document title itself) is a four-DISCRETE-resistor difference amplifier in which t is the tolerance of the gain-setting network. The record asserts, without a page, that the same algebra governs stray asymmetry - trace length and width, via count, each input's neighbourhood. It does not: t has no counterpart in a bare trace pair, and with ina333 p16 putting in-amp input impedance at approximately 100 Gohm, essentially no common-mode current flows in a mismatched series trace resistance, so a bare pair converts essentially nothing at DC. The headline claim that CMRR at this interface is set by input-path mismatch and NOT by the amplifier CMRR spec is therefore false for the case this record keys - an in-amp fed from a low-impedance balanced source with no fitted input network, where the internally trimmed network is the limit. The ledger supports the narrower true claim that slyt226 p1 actually makes: a passive network FITTED at the input, and mismatched shunt RC over frequency, degrade CMRR. That is weaker than what the record claims. (3) The envelope runs backwards. vcm_v is capped at 5 V and envelope_note reasons that on a high-common-mode input the amplifier's own input range binds first and path mismatch stops being the limit. The converted error is Vcm times the fractional mismatch, so it GROWS with common mode, and the cited topology - a discrete difference amplifier with attenuating input dividers - exists precisely to run at high common mode, which is where resistor matching matters most. The bound is too narrow and its stated mechanism is wrong. TO PASS: state the gain condition on the 40 dB case, restrict the (G+1)/(4t) law to a fitted resistor network, carry the stray-asymmetry claim as the shunt-RC-over-frequency mechanism slyt226 supports rather than as the same algebra, and drop or invert the vcm bound.

in-leakage-symmetry-and-guarding.note: Re-read 01258b p12, p13, p14 and ina333 p16 visually. The p12 citation holds in full: Figure 26 is the Thevenin source with RP1 to RP4 to all other nearby voltage nodes including ground, the typical values are RP approximately 1000 Gohm at low humidity and contamination and approximately 1 Gohm at high humidity and contamination, guard rings have no solder mask so the leakage flows into them, the ring is biased at the same voltage as the sensitive node and needs to be driven by a low impedance source, and Figure 28 is the SMD unity-gain-buffer ring. The ina333 p16 citation is honest - 100 Gohm and +-70 pA are on that page and are used only to set the scale. REFUTED on the page number, which is the test this fails outright. Page 13 carries only Figures 29 to 32 (unity-gain buffer, non-inverting gain, transimpedance equivalent circuits), the VOS-across-RP2 argument and the sentence the leakage current is typically reduced by a factor of about 1000. The other two claims the record attributes to p13 are one page over, on p14, under a heading the record folds into its p13 section title: Guard Rings on Both PCB Surfaces - For op amps in through-hole packages (e.g., PDIP), guard rings are needed on both top and bottom surfaces; Any jumper traces ... connected to traces with guard rings, also need guard rings around the jumper traces. It is better, when possible, to avoid jumper traces for critical nodes. Two of the three claims in that one citation note, and two of the three items in rule.guard_rules, are sourced to a page that does not contain them. Second, independent defect: the envelope caps rsource_ohm at 1 Mohm while envelope_note itself says that at and above 1 Mohm an actively driven guard, not symmetry, is the prescribed technique - so rule.guard_regime and rule.guard_rules, half the record, describe behaviour outside the envelope in which the record claims to apply. The arithmetic behind the bound is sound (a 1 Gohm humid parasitic from a 3.3 V net onto a 175 ohm node is about 0.6 uV, onto a 1 Mohm node about 3 mV), so the number is defensible; the range it gates is not. TO PASS: split the citation into p13 (VOS argument, factor of about 1000) and p14 (both surfaces, jumpers), and either raise the rsource ceiling to cover the guard regime the record prescribes or split the two regimes into two records with adjoining envelopes. Noted but NOT the ground: every guard ring in this app note (Figures 28 to 33) is driven from the output of a single-ended op amp at the one sensitive node potential, and the record transplants that to a differential pair whose two inputs differ by the signal without saying what a differential guard is driven from - at 20 mV of signal on a 1.65 V common mode a single ring at the common-mode potential is within 10 mV of both nodes, so this is an incompleteness rather than an error. The equal-neighbourhood symmetry regime is the record's own reasoning and is on none of the cited pages, but the source notes do not claim otherwise.

in-aggressor-separation.note: Re-read 01258b p17 and p4 and ina333 p20 visually, plus 01258b p15 and p18 to test the uncited rules. The transcriptions are the most accurate of this batch. 01258b p17 callout 6 is verbatim (Sensor traces are separated from power (top layer) and digital (bottom layer) traces to reduce crosstalk), callout 1 is verbatim (The Difference Amplifier is as close to the sensor as possible, and is on the opposite PCB surface from the PICmicro microcontroller. This minimizes electrical and thermal crosstalk between the two active devices), callout 7 is verbatim for the MCP9800 power traces. ina333 p20 s10.1 is verbatim (Keep traces short and, when possible, use a printed-circuit-board (PCB) ground plane with surface-mount components placed as close to the device pins as possible. Place a 0.1-uF bypass capacitor closely across the supply pins), and Figure 40 does show VIN- and VIN+ entering as an equal-width parallel pair with nothing between them and the gain resistor straddling both RG pads. REFUTED because the two load-bearing rule fields are witnessed by no page in this ledger. (1) rule.reference states route the pair together over UNBROKEN reference copper - no split, slot or void under the pair or under the input pins. No cited page says this. ina333 p20 says only, when possible, use a PCB ground plane - a weaker claim, and hedged. The 01258b p17 callouts say nothing about plane continuity, and I checked p15 (CROSSED TRACES, GUARD RINGS, GUARD PLANE, Examples 3 to 5) and p18 for a statement of it: there is none in the app note. What p18 does show is the opposite emphasis - Figure 41, 3rd Layer Ground Plane, with a deliberate FR4 gap splitting the reference between the amplifier side and the sensor side (callout 13, same function as callout 10), bridged only by a narrow ground plane extension (callout 14) and with digital traces crossing under it through series resistors in the gap (callout 19). The vendor trades plane continuity for thermal isolation on its own precision reference design. Stated flatly as a rule, with no page and with the ledger's only worked example cutting the other way. (2) rule.aggressors names the amplifier's OWN OUTPUT as a principal aggressor alongside the supply entry. No cited page names it. The vendor design example names power and the microcontroller (callouts 1, 6, 7) and 01258b p12 to p13 in fact prescribes surrounding the sensitive input with copper driven from VOUT. Plausible reasoning at high forward gain, and the coupling_budget arithmetic is right (5 uV in 3 V is under 2 ppm), but it is derivation stated as vendor practice inside a prose paragraph introduced with Vendor practice, read from a precision sensor board. TO PASS: demote rule.reference to what ina333 p20 supports (use a ground plane where possible) or cite a reference-continuity source, and mark the output-as-aggressor and the coupling ratio explicitly as derived. Minor: the p4 citation drops the source's hedge - low profile components MAY have the additional advantage of reduced electrical crosstalk - and the record renders it as have.
